coverage_of_risk.rationale: The app wrote no tests at all, and its riskiest logic (filtering, pagination, moves aggregation, sorting, name formatting) has zero coverage beyond the external acceptance suite.

evidence: app/ — zero test files; grep for test/spec/vitest/jest matched only .next/ build artifacts
behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: No tests exist, so there is no behavioural (or any other) coverage to evaluate.

evidence: app/lib/data.js:94-108 — pokemonRefsToSpecies refactor (alternate-form cutoff, dedup, hidden flag) would pass silently with bugs

regression_power.rationale: With no tests in app/, any regression in data transformation, URL state, or sorting would ship unnoticed once the acceptance suite is no longer run against this code.

signal_to_noise.rationale: Per the rubric, the absence of tests is neutral here; there is no noise, but also no signal.

findings.issue: No test infrastructure at all: no test script, no test runner dependency, zero test files in app/.
findings.suggestion: Add Vitest (per current Next.js testing guide) with unit tests for lib/format.js and lib/data.js, and a `test` script wired into CI alongside the acceptance suite.

findings.issue: Filtering and pagination logic (humanized-name substring match, type-in-either-slot, generation membership, parseInt page clamp, 48-per-page slicing, queryString default omission at lines 15-23) is entirely untested.
findings.suggestion: Extract the filter/match/paginate step into a pure function in lib/ and unit-test edge cases: empty q, invalid type vs invalid generation, page beyond totalPages, page=0 or non-numeric.

findings.issue: buildMoves is the densest logic in the app (per-method dedupe keeping min level, method ordering comparator at lines 99-105, default game = highest order, level-then-name sort) and is untested.
findings.suggestion: Extract buildMoves into lib/moves.js as a pure function over fetched records and add table-driven tests for method order, dedupe, missing records, and ?game= selection.

findings.issue: Descending sort reverses the tie-broken array, so descending by Power also reverses the move-name tie order; missing-last logic is subtle and untested.
findings.suggestion: Extract sortRows to lib and test ascending/descending per column, missing values last, and tie behavior explicitly.

findings.issue: pokemonRefsToSpecies silently drops entries whose species lookup fails and handles wrapped vs bare refs plus the extra() hidden flag; a refactor here breaks ability hidden markers and alternate-form exclusion invisibly.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test with fixtures containing ids >= 10000, duplicate ids, missing species, and ability-shaped entries with is_hidden.

findings.issue: Pure helpers (humanize edge cases like empty segments, dexNumber padding, latest-English flavor text, \f collapsing) are the cheapest tests in the codebase and none exist.
findings.suggestion: Add a small Vitest suite covering each helper's spec-defined edge cases; these encode the SPEC's naming and formatting rules.

findings.issue: Debounced search (300ms), URL replace/push, page reset on filter change, and input re-sync on external URL changes are untested interactive behaviors.
findings.suggestion: Add a component/browser test that types, waits for debounce, asserts the URL, and verifies filter changes reset page to 1.

findings.issue: API caching semantics (404→null, non-ok→throw, cache eviction on rejection, globalThis store) are untested; a refactor could cache rejected promises or drop 404-null handling.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test apiJson against a stubbed fetch covering 404, 500, network error, and cache-hit paths.

findings.issue: species.evolution_chain.url is dereferenced unguarded and not-found paths (excluded types at app/types/[name]/page.jsx:23-24, invalid names on all routes) have no tests; a chainless species would produce a 500 instead of a rendered page.
findings.suggestion: Guard optional relations and add a test (or at least manual check) for the not-found and degenerate-data paths on every route.

summary: The app contains no tests of its own — no runner, no script, no test files — despite being full of hand-rolled filtering, pagination, sorting and data-transformation logic that would be cheap to unit-test (much of it is already pure functions in lib/). Once the acceptance suite is retired, any refactor of the data layer or URL-state handling can silently regress search, pagination, move-table ordering, or alternate-form exclusion. Adding Vitest coverage for lib/format.js, lib/data.js, and the extracted filter/sort/moves logic would close most of the gap.
